From: Diane Park <diane.park@medilane.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@medilane.com
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: sealed operator manifest + locality declaration

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of our SIG + CAIQ intake we need a short, signed "operator manifest" that confirms the physical region of hosting for the Redwood Private deployment for our pilot (prod data, EU-only). Specifically we need two items:

- A one-page sealed manifest stating: primary hosting region, whether backup / DR nodes cross borders, and the keystore custody model.
- An operator roster CSV with names and roles for the operator accounts that can access tenant keystores (Dev/Ops/SRE).

Can you confirm you can provide these artifacts (PDF + CSV) and a link where Medilane compliance can download them? Target deadline is COB Friday so our compliance team can close the SIG questionnaire.

Thanks,
Diane Park
Head of Vendor Risk | MediLane Health
[d] +44 20 5555 0123
[Attachment: medilane_sig_scope.pdf (PDF)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Diane Park <diane.park@medilane.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: sealed operator manifest + locality declaration

Hi Diane —

Appreciate the scope. We can produce a sealed manifest and the operator roster. Quick clarifications so we include precisely what you need:

1) By "sealed" do you require a PDF with a designated signatory from Redwood (legal or security) and a timestamp, or is an uploaded PDF + DocuSign link sufficient?
2) For "backup / DR nodes cross borders" — do you want the exact fallback region names (e.g., eu-west-1 -> us-east-1) or a yes/no statement plus fallbacks only triggered under explicit contractual conditions?
3) Keystore custody: we will include KMS partitioning and whether Redwood or the customer holds the root key. Do you also need the HSM vendor name listed?

We'll prepare a draft and circulate internally this afternoon. Marissa / Rishi — looping you in for ops + legal signoff item: can you review the manifest draft and the CSV before I send to MediLane?

Jonas Weber
Director, Security Programs | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 15:18:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Request: sealed operator manifest + locality declaration

Folks — forwarding Diane's ask. Short turnaround (COB Fri). Draft outline below, please comment inline or reply with edits:

--- draft outline for sealed manifest ---
- Header: Redwood Inference — Sealed Operator Manifest
- Statement: Primary hosting region for account(s) scoped to pilot -> eu-west-1 (Frankfurt).
- DR/Fallback: Secondary standby nodes exist in eu-central-1 and will NOT fail over to outside EU under normal failover; cross-border fallback to us-east-1 only under catastrophe and subject to contractually agreed escalations.
- Keystore custody: Customer-managed envelope encryption (customer KMS key) + Redwood HSM for operational signing. Root key custody = MediLane; operational key escrow policy referenced.
- Signatory: Redwood Chief Security Officer or Legal ops sign-off line + timestamp + PDF seal.

Operator roster CSV columns (required): name, role, email, access_level, operator_id, last_mfa_assertion_date

Can you confirm the wording on the DR clause is conservative enough? Rishi, should we avoid listing vendor HSM brand in this doc (we sometimes do in public artifacts)? Marissa — any legal phrasing preferences for "catastrophe" vs "emergency"?

Thanks — I can stitch the draft into the PDF once we have sign-off.

Jonas

Diane —

Attached please find the sealed operator manifest and the operator roster CSV you requested. Short summary of key commitments (pulled from the PDF):

- Primary region: eu-west-1 (Frankfurt) — customer production data stored and processed in EU footprint for the MediLane pilot.
- DR posture: standby replicas in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt/Frankfurt-2). Cross-border failover to us-east-1 is explicitly reserved for "catastrophic continuity events" and will only occur with documented approval from MediLane and a formal incident review.
- Keystore custody: MediLane holds the root KMS key; Redwood manages operational keys under an escrow agreement.
- Signatory: Sealed and timestamped by Redwood Chief Security Officer (Emily Park).

Delivery: PDF is uploaded to our secure drive and shared with MediLane compliance (link below). We've also initiated a DocuSign envelope for the manifest (for formal signature trace).
